title: Vetala Story 11: The Two Brothers and the Woman Who Chose
summary: The Vetala whispered: 'Listen, O King, to the choice of Princess Sulochana!'...
keywords: vetala story 11: the two brothers and the woman who chose
full_text:
King Vikramaditya cut down the corpse, hoisted it onto his shoulders, and resumed his march.

The Vetala whispered: 'Listen, O King, to the choice of Princess Sulochana!'

In the city of Vidisha lived two twin brothers, Shurasena and Gunadhara. Shurasena was an athletic warrior of colossal strength, capable of wrestling tigers with his bare hands, while Gunadhara was a poet, scholar, and statesman, whose verses charmed kings.

Both brothers fell deeply in love with Princess Sulochana, daughter of the local ruler.

The king declared: 'Let the princess choose between the two brothers according to her own heart!'

The warrior Shurasena stepped forward, boasting: 'Princess! Marry me! With my mighty sword and colossal muscles, I can defeat armies, conquer kingdoms, and shield you from all physical peril!'

The scholar Gunadhara stepped forward, speaking softly: 'Princess! I possess neither colossal muscles nor an army. But I possess a mind that seeks truth, a heart that listens with patience, and words that bring peace in the dark hour of sorrow.'

The princess chose the scholar Gunadhara, and they were wed.

Shortly after, a foreign invader besieged the city. Gunadhara used his diplomatic brilliance to negotiate a peaceful treaty, saving the city without spilling blood.

Here the Vetala asked: 'King Vikramaditya! Did the princess choose with wisdom, or did she err in rejecting the mighty warrior? Answer, or your head will burst into fragments!'

Vikramaditya replied: 'She chose with supreme wisdom. Physical strength is a perishable gift that fades with age and can be broken by a stray arrow; but wisdom, intellect, and gentle patience grow richer with the years and preserve the household through every season of life.'

'True, O King!' chuckled the Vetala, and soared back into the tree.
moral: A companion of intellect and gentle manners provides enduring happiness where raw strength falters.
